evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Jokowi as the speaking president and policy director.
contrary_evidence: Rhetoric does not prove implementation.
Later reporting still found legal and administrative conflict around investment and labor rules.

evidence.title: Pemerintah Alihkan Subsidi BBM Agar Lebih Tepat Sasaran
evidence.claim: Jokowi announced the reallocation of fuel subsidy funds because more than 70% of the subsidy benefited people who could afford it; the subsidy and compensation budget rose from Rp152.5 trillion to Rp502.4 trillion, with targeted BLT and wage support added.
evidence.locator: body paragraphs after the dateline and the quoted presidential remarks
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential announcement with concrete fiscal figures and policy rationale.
evidence.period_fit: Squarely in September 2022 during the fuel-price shock response.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Jokowi and his cabinet as the policy makers announcing the transfer.
contrary_evidence: Higher fuel prices imposed real costs on households.
The policy was also a response to budget pressure, not pure distributive generosity.

evidence.title: Untuk Melindungi Masyarakat Miskin dan Rentan Miskin, Pemerintah Alokasikan Dana BLT BBM Rp24,17 Triliun
evidence.claim: The finance ministry said the fuel-subsidy transfer package totaled Rp24.17 trillion and included BLT BBM, wage subsidies, and local-government transport support to shield poor and vulnerable households from price shocks.
evidence.locator: opening paragraphs and quoted ministerial remarks
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official finance-ministry release with detailed budget and beneficiary figures.
evidence.period_fit: Directly describes 2022 crisis response after the fuel-price adjustment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to Jokowi’s government via the finance ministry and presidential policy response.
contrary_evidence: Effectiveness is asserted by the ministry, not independently measured here.
The package was reactive to a price increase the government itself imposed.

evidence.title: Monetary Policy Review - December 2022
evidence.claim: Bank Indonesia said CPI inflation ended 2022 at 5.51 percent after subsidized fuel prices were adjusted in September 2022, and that close Government-BI coordination produced a front-loaded, pre-emptive response with core inflation at 3.36 percent.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Central-bank report with direct inflation and policy-response data.
evidence.period_fit: End-of-2022 macro and policy assessment for the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Only partially attributable to Jokowi because BI is independent, but the report explicitly credits government-BI coordination after the fuel-price move.
contrary_evidence: Inflation still exceeded the target band.
The central bank, not the president alone, drove monetary stabilization.

evidence.title: Indonesia GDP Growth Rate 5.31 Percent (2022)
evidence.claim: BPS said Indonesia’s economy grew 5.31 percent in 2022, GDP per capita reached Rp71.0 million or US$4,783.9, and exports were the strongest growth component.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official national statistics release with year-end macro figures.
evidence.period_fit: Directly measures 2022 macro performance.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to Jokowi’s government, but also shaped by reopening and commodity prices.
contrary_evidence: The result reflects strong external commodity conditions and post-COVID reopening as well as domestic policy.
Growth alone does not prove broad-based prosperity.

evidence.title: August 2022: The unemployment rate was 5.86 percent and The average labour wage was 3.07 milion rupiahs per month
evidence.claim: BPS reported that August 2022 unemployment was 5.86 percent, the number of employed people increased by 4.25 million from August 2021, and the formal sector share rose to 40.69 percent.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official labor-market release with year-over-year figures.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 labor-market outcome.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Macro outcome partly attributable to Jokowi’s government, but not exclusively; labor markets also reflected post-pandemic recovery.
contrary_evidence: The release does not isolate policy causation.
Underemployment and wage levels still leave room for concern about job quality.

evidence.title: In September 2022, the poor population percentage was up to 9.57 percent.
evidence.claim: BPS reported poverty at 9.57 percent in September 2022, up 0.03 percentage points from March 2022 but down from September 2021, with rural poverty at 12.36 percent and urban poverty at 7.53 percent.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official national-statistics release with household-poverty and regional breakdowns.
evidence.period_fit: Directly measures 2022 household welfare.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to Jokowi’s policy mix, but the report also reflects inherited poverty structure and macro shocks.
contrary_evidence: Poverty improved versus September 2021, so the year does not show simple deterioration.
The data do not by themselves prove government causation.

evidence.title: Gini Ratio in September 2022 was 0.381
evidence.claim: BPS reported a September 2022 Gini ratio of 0.381, unchanged from September 2021 and down from March 2022; the bottom 40 percent accounted for 18.24 percent of expenditure.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official inequality release with national and regional breakdowns.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 distribution outcome.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Only partly attributable to Jokowi; inequality outcomes also reflect long-run structure and external conditions.
contrary_evidence: The level still indicates meaningful inequality.
Stable inequality is not the same as broad-based gain.

evidence.title: Indonesia Economic Prospects (IEP), June 2022: Financial Deepening for Stronger Growth and Sustainable Recovery
evidence.claim: The World Bank said Indonesia needed deeper financial markets, noted the 2022 budget reduced extraordinary COVID support and refocused on health and the war in Ukraine, and recommended tax reforms, a better business environment, greener downstream industries, and financial deepening to sustain growth.
evidence.locator: key findings section with ten numbered findings
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official World Bank country report with explicit policy recommendations and macro context.
evidence.period_fit: Mid-2022 assessment of the same year’s policy stance and outlook.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government-level attribution under Jokowi, with specific spending and reform choices in his administration.
contrary_evidence: Much of the text is analytical and prescriptive rather than a record of implementation.
Some macro improvement was due to commodity and reopening effects.

evidence.title: New Financing Will Support Indonesia to Improve and Protect Human Capital
evidence.claim: The World Bank approved a $350 million loan to improve human capital through income protection, expanded health access, healthier behavior, and more effective government spending; it said Indonesia’s Human Capital Index improved from 0.50 to 0.54 between 2010 and 2020 but remained below peers.
evidence.locator: opening paragraphs and key bullet points
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official World Bank financing announcement with explicit human-capital metrics.
evidence.period_fit: Directly relevant to 2022 productivity and welfare policy.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government-level attribution under Jokowi’s administration; the loan reflects state policy rather than a private-sector outcome.
contrary_evidence: The improvement in HCI predates 2022.
The report says Indonesia still lagged peer countries.

evidence.title: 2022 Corruption Perceptions Index - Explore Indonesia
evidence.claim: Transparency International’s 2022 CPI gave Indonesia a score of 34/100 and rank 110/180, down 4 points from 2021, and said anti-corruption efforts had stagnated.
evidence.locator: country score panel and Asia-Pacific commentary
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary CPI publication from the source organization that owns the index.
evidence.period_fit: Measures the 2022 corruption environment and policy trajectory.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to Jokowi’s administration, but CPI is a perception index and not a case-level finding.
contrary_evidence: Perception scores are not direct proof of specific ruler orders.
The CPI blends expert and business perceptions across institutions, not just presidential conduct.

evidence.title: Indonesia issues emergency regulation to replace jobs law
evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Jokowi signed an emergency regulation to replace a court-flawed jobs law, arguing global economic uncertainty justified the move; critics said it bypassed proper parliamentary debate, while the government said the law was needed for legal certainty and investment.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting with named officials and direct quotes, republished on a commercial site.
evidence.period_fit: Late-2022 ruler action directly affecting investment rules and labor regulation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Jokowi as signatory and public defender of the decree.
contrary_evidence: Government said global uncertainty and the court deadline required a legal fix.
Supporters said it reduced investment uncertainty; opponents said it undermined consultation and labor and environmental protections.

evidence.title: Indonesia to review minimum wage rules after protests over fuel price hike
evidence.claim: After nationwide protests over the September 2022 petrol price hike, the president’s office said Indonesia would review minimum wage and other labor rules; Reuters also reported that Jokowi had raised subsidised fuel prices by 30% to rein in the subsidy budget.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting with direct references to the presidential office and the fuel-price decision.
evidence.period_fit: Direct September 2022 policy response to an economic shock.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Jokowi’s fuel-price decision and the presidential office’s subsequent review order.
contrary_evidence: The policy was framed as fiscal necessity rather than distributive generosity.
The article shows both popular backlash and administrative response, not clean welfare success.

evidence.title: Jokowi orders seventh Cabinet reshuffle
evidence.claim: The Jakarta Post reported that analysts saw Jokowi’s June 2022 reshuffle as more political than technocratic, aimed at keeping coalition partners happy and filling the cabinet with loyalists; Jokowi said the new trade minister would oversee domestic goods supply and the agrarian minister land acquisition for the new capital.
evidence.locator: middle and later paragraphs on cabinet motives and appointments
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Local-paper analysis with named analysts, direct quotes, and contemporaneous appointment details.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the 2022 ruler period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Jokowi’s cabinet choices.
contrary_evidence: The presidency presented the reshuffle as a normal appointment decree and a way to refresh the cabinet.
The article reflects analyst interpretation, not a formal finding of improper motive.

evidence.title: Tax Revenue Reaches 110.06 Percent
evidence.claim: Tax income had reached 110.06 percent of target by 14 December 2022 and grew 41.93 percent year over year; Sri Mulyani said this reflected good economic recovery, rising commodities, and reform of the tax law.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official presidential-secretariat republication of finance-ministry data and quoted explanation.
evidence.period_fit: End-of-2022 fiscal-performance evidence for the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Jokowi’s administration through the finance ministry and tax policy apparatus.
contrary_evidence: Commodity prices materially boosted receipts, so this is not purely a structural-policy effect.
The article reports achievement against target, not distributional quality.

evidence.title: Pemerintah Perkuat Kebijakan Satu Data dengan Registrasi Sosial Ekonomi
evidence.claim: Jokowi said strengthening one-data policy through Regsosek 2022 was necessary so the census could cover all residents, and the government asked BPS to run national data collection and update separated welfare datasets.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential-meeting recap with named presidential instruction and implementation details.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 ruler action on social-registry targeting.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Jokowi as the president who chaired the meeting and issued the instruction; execution ran through BPS and coordinating ministries.
contrary_evidence: This is a targeting/infrastructure measure, not proof of downstream welfare gains.
The page reports intent and data integration, not full nationwide completion.

evidence.title: The social and economic impact of COVID-19 on households in Indonesia
evidence.claim: A second survey conducted in February-March 2022 at the request of the Indonesian Ministry of Finance captured longitudinal data from 10,922 households and examined benefits and gaps in social protection, with special focus on children, women, people with disability, and vulnerable communities.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent survey summary from UNICEF with explicit methodology, sample size, and policy focus.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 household evidence with pandemic-era policy relevance.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government-requested survey under Jokowi’s administration, but the findings are diagnostic rather than direct presidential action.
contrary_evidence: This is a survey, not an evaluation of causality for specific programs.
It highlights social-protection gaps as well as protections.

evidence.title: Penyaluran BLT BBM Capai 95,9 Persen
evidence.claim: Jokowi said the BLT BBM disbursement had reached 95.9 percent, or 19.7 million beneficiaries, and that the BSU had reached 48.3 percent; the government framed both as social assistance to maintain purchasing power during the fuel-subsidy transfer.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential visit report with exact rollout figures and stated purpose.
evidence.period_fit: Direct September 2022 shock-response implementation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Jokowi and his government as the public face of the rollout.
contrary_evidence: Reported coverage is administrative rollout, not independent impact evaluation.
The policy responded to a fuel-price increase and household pressure.

evidence.title: Untuk Melindungi Masyarakat Miskin dan Rentan Miskin, Pemerintah Alokasikan Dana BLT BBM Rp24,17 Triliun
evidence.claim: The finance ministry said the fuel-subsidy transfer package totaled Rp24.17 trillion, including BSU for 14.6 million workers and BLT BBM for 20.65 million beneficiary families, plus local-government spending for social protection, jobs, and transport support.
evidence.locator: opening paragraphs / ministerial remarks in the article
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official finance-ministry release with concrete fiscal and beneficiary figures.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 fiscal response to the fuel-price shock.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government-level attribution under Jokowi’s administration through the finance ministry.
contrary_evidence: The ministry’s own framing is promotional and not an independent impact evaluation.
The package was reactive to an adverse price shock rather than a standalone welfare expansion.

evidence.title: Indonesia Targets Low Vaccination Areas to Tackle Decline in Childhood Immunization
evidence.claim: WHO reported that Indonesia achieved 94.6 percent full immunization coverage in 2022, above the national target of 94.1 percent, and that the government mounted the BIAN catch-up campaign in 2022 reaching 26.5 million children with measles-rubella vaccines, 1.3 million with polio vaccines, and 2 million with DTP-HB-Hib vaccines.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: WHO country office page with 2022 outcome figures and explicit government campaign description.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective on 2022 health-service delivery and vaccination response.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government-led implementation under Jokowi, through the health ministry; the page also notes remaining low-coverage outbreaks.
contrary_evidence: The same source says outbreaks persisted in low-coverage areas.
Coverage gains do not prove equal access across all provinces.

evidence.title: Kementerian Kesehatan Rilis Hasil Survei Status Gizi Indonesia (SSGI) tahun 2022
evidence.claim: Indonesia’s stunting rate fell by 2.8 percentage points from 2021 to 2022, and the ministry linked the decline to interventions for adolescents, pregnant women, and children under 23 months, including ANC, iron tablets, complementary feeding, growth monitoring, exclusive breastfeeding, and more immunization.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official ministry summary of the 2022 SSGI with specific intervention pathways and target groups.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective on the target year 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government-level attribution under Jokowi, through the health ministry and national stunting strategy.
contrary_evidence: This is a ministry summary rather than independent validation.
The target of 14 percent by 2024 had not yet been reached.

evidence.title: Recovering from the impacts of COVID-19 school closures in Indonesia
evidence.claim: The World Bank said school closures affected 68.8 million students and caused estimated learning loss of 0.9 to 1.2 years; after technical discussions with Indonesia’s education and religious ministries, it said the government and schools made strides through simplified curricula, teacher development, after-school tutoring, EdTech, and psychosocial support.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: World Bank analyst blog with concrete estimates and named ministry interactions, but not a formal evaluation report.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 recovery context with retrospective learning-loss estimates.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government-level attribution under Jokowi’s administration; the interventions were implemented through education and religious-ministry channels.
contrary_evidence: The page says learning losses remained substantial.
It is a blog summary, not a case-by-case implementation audit.

evidence.title: The impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on children’s learning in Indonesia
evidence.claim: The pandemic had a negative impact on learning across all education levels in Indonesia, and the brief focused on out-of-school children and those at risk of dropping out from socio-economically disadvantaged families.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent UNICEF issue brief centered on the education risks facing vulnerable groups.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 context for learning and youth welfare.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly contextual rather than a direct ruler action, but it defines the inherited learning-loss burden faced by Jokowi’s administration.
contrary_evidence: This is a context brief rather than a policy evaluation.
It documents harm and risk, not delivery success.

evidence.title: Rincian Harta Kekayaan Presiden Jokowi yang Naik Rp 7,8 Miliar Selama 2021
evidence.claim: Kompas reported that Jokowi filed his LHKPN on 24 February 2022, disclosing total assets of Rp71.47 billion for the 2021 reporting period, up from the prior year.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Secondary reporting on a public asset declaration with concrete figures and filing date.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the 2022 period, based on a filing made in February 2022 and reported in April 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Jokowi as a public disclosure of his own assets; not an external audit.
contrary_evidence: Self-reporting is not independent proof of honesty beyond compliance.
The article does not test source-of-wealth legitimacy or undisclosed conflicts.

evidence.title: Two Newly-Inaugurated Ministers Have Excellent Track Records, President Jokowi Says
evidence.claim: Jokowi said the 15 June 2022 ministerial appointments were based on track record, experience, and managerial skills, and he publicly explained why he chose Zulkifli Hasan and Hadi Tjahjanto.
evidence.locator: opening paragraphs and the quoted explanation of appointment criteria
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential-secretariat transcript of the president’s stated justification for appointments.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 appointment decision.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Jokowi as the appointing president.
contrary_evidence: The source is the president’s own explanation, so it is self-justifying.
Independent reporting in the same week argued the reshuffle was political and coalition-driven.

reasons.reason: Self-justifying appointment explanation; it is Jokowi's stated rationale, but it is not independent proof of integrity or lack of patronage.

evidence.title: Reshuffle helps coalition close ranks ahead of polls
evidence.claim: The Jakarta Post reported that analysts saw Jokowi’s June 2022 reshuffle as a way to keep the coalition unified and install more loyalists, with the palace using the event to show there were no fractures in the ruling bloc.
evidence.locator: middle paragraphs describing analyst assessments and coalition dynamics
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous reporting with named analysts and direct quotes, but still interpretive.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Jokowi’s cabinet choices and coalition management.
contrary_evidence: Analyst interpretation is not a legal finding of self-dealing.
The article also notes the reshuffle’s stated public-utility rationale.

reasons.reason: Analyst interpretation about coalition management is inferential and should not be treated as a factual finding of self-dealing.

evidence.title: How Jokowi uses deputy ministers to strengthen his grip on power
evidence.claim: The Jakarta Post said experts viewed the expansion of deputy minister posts as a political bargaining chip used by Jokowi to consolidate power and reward loyalists as he entered the twilight of his second term.
evidence.locator: opening and middle paragraphs on cabinet expansion and expert commentary
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous reporting with named analysts and specific appointment details.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Jokowi’s appointment choices and cabinet structure.
contrary_evidence: Expert commentary is not a judicial finding.
The piece describes political consolidation, not direct personal enrichment.

reasons.reason: This is another inferential reshuffle commentary item in the same event family; keep only as context, not as proof of nepotism or corruption.

evidence.title: Indonesia issues emergency regulation to replace jobs law
evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Jokowi signed an emergency regulation to replace a court-flawed jobs law, arguing global economic uncertainty justified the move, while critics said it bypassed proper parliamentary debate.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting with named actor, direct quote, and contemporaneous criticism.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 ruler action.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Jokowi as signatory and public defender of the regulation.
contrary_evidence: The government gave a legal-necessity rationale tied to economic uncertainty.
The reporting does not by itself prove deceit, but it does show a process-bypassing move.

evidence.title: On Police Murder Case, President Jokowi: Find the Truth
evidence.claim: Jokowi told investigators to settle the Brigadier J murder case thoroughly, warned that nothing must be covered up, and said they should find the truth.
evidence.locator: opening paragraphs and the quoted presidential remarks
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential statement published by the Cabinet Secretariat, with clear quoted language.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the 2022 period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Jokowi as head of state and commander over the relevant institutions.
contrary_evidence: This concerns a police murder case, not his own private conduct.
Public exhortation to find the truth does not itself prove full accountability in practice.

evidence.title: Soal Tragedi Kanjuruhan, Presiden: Usut Tuntas, Beri Sanksi yang Bersalah
evidence.claim: After the Kanjuruhan tragedy, Jokowi said the case should be investigated to the end and that those found guilty should be sanctioned; he said he had already ordered relevant ministers and police chiefs to handle it.
evidence.locator: opening paragraphs and quoted presidential remarks
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential statement on a major state failure, published by the Cabinet Secretariat.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Jokowi as the head of government directing the response.
contrary_evidence: The source shows his response to the disaster, not whether underlying abuse was prevented.
It is an accountability posture rather than proof of the final investigative outcome.

evidence.title: Enam Fokus Utama untuk RAPBN Tahun 2022
evidence.claim: Jokowi set six APBN 2022 priorities, including health, social protection, human resources, infrastructure, decentralization, and zero-based budgeting, and framed the budget as supporting recovery and structural reform.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official presidential budget speech summary with specific budget priorities and allocations.
evidence.period_fit: Pre-period program document for 2022 policy direction; directly governs 2022 budgeting and implementation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Jokowi as the budget-setting head of government.
contrary_evidence: This is a stated program and budget plan, not proof of delivery by itself.

evidence.title: Presiden Jokowi Instruksikan Jajaran Antisipasi Krisis Pangan dan Energi
evidence.claim: Jokowi ordered his cabinet to anticipate food and energy crises, warned that the world was not in a normal condition, and urged production and reserve planning.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential instructions recorded by the Cabinet Secretariat on the day of the meeting.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 fit.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Jokowi; this is his cabinet instruction.
contrary_evidence: The source shows warning and direction, not outcome by itself.

evidence.title: Two Newly-Inaugurated Ministers Have Excellent Track Records, President Jokowi Says
evidence.claim: Jokowi said the 2022 appointments of Zulkifli Hasan and Hadi Tjahjanto were based on track record, experience, and managerial skill for the problems he wanted solved.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official post-inauguration explanation of minister selection criteria.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 fit.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Jokowi’s appointment choices and stated rationale.
contrary_evidence: The source records Jokowi’s justification; it does not independently verify the appointees’ competence.

evidence.title: How Jokowi uses deputy ministers to strengthen his grip on power
evidence.claim: Analysts said Jokowi expanded deputy-minister posts to accommodate loyalists and consolidate power within the coalition.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reputable national newspaper reporting with named analysts, but the core judgment is interpretive.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 fit.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attribution is inferential: it concerns Jokowi’s reshuffle choices and coalition management, not direct proof of his intent.
contrary_evidence: The same move can also be read as coalition management rather than pure patronage.

evidence.title: President Jokowi Pushes For Down Streaming of Mining Products
evidence.claim: Jokowi said the government was committed to downstream mining, wanted value added in Indonesia rather than raw-material exports, and cited the nickel smelter policy as a successful example.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential remarks with concrete policy example and quantified export change.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 fit.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Jokowi’s policy direction and repeated public advocacy.
contrary_evidence: Commodity prices and private investment also contributed to the outcome; the source does not isolate Jokowi’s causal share.

evidence.title: President Jokowi Hands Over 2023 Budget Implementation List, Transfer to Regions, Village Funds
evidence.claim: Jokowi framed the 2023 budget as an instrument to maintain stability and continue recovery, structural reform, and social protection, and told officials to realize APBN and APBD spending.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official budget handover statement with explicit spending priorities and implementation instruction.
evidence.period_fit: Late-2022 budget implementation and planning for 2023; fits the target year as end-of-period evidence.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Jokowi as the budget handover speaker and policy setter.
contrary_evidence: This is still a plan/implementation directive, not proof that agencies delivered the intended results.

evidence.title: President Jokowi Explains Development in Nusantara New Capital
evidence.claim: Jokowi said infrastructure development in the core Nusantara area had started, including raw-water supply, and that ministry and presidential-palace construction would begin in December.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential update on a flagship project with concrete construction milestones.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 fit.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Jokowi as the project’s political sponsor and public decision-maker.
contrary_evidence: Construction start does not by itself show completion or durable success by year-end.

evidence.title: Indonesia issues emergency regulation to replace jobs law
evidence.claim: Jokowi signed an emergency regulation replacing the jobs law to preserve legal certainty and investment prospects amid global uncertainty; critics said it bypassed proper parliamentary debate.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting is strong for the fact pattern and includes both government rationale and critical response.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 fit.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Jokowi and his economic team; the source also shows the stated strategic motive.
contrary_evidence: Critics said the move bypassed proper parliamentary debate and emergency conditions were disputed.

evidence.title: IMF Staff Completes 2023 Article IV Mission to Indonesia
evidence.claim: IMF staff said Indonesia’s 2022 GDP grew 5.3 percent, the 2022 budget deficit was 2.4 percent of GDP, and higher fuel prices and revenue gains helped contain the subsidy bill.
evidence.locator: press-release bullet points and quoted assessment
evidence.source_confidence_reason: IMF staff press release provides a concise retrospective macro assessment with specific quantified outcomes.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective assessment of 2022 outcomes; fits the target year directly.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attribution is partial: Jokowi’s fiscal and energy-price choices mattered, but commodity prices and global conditions were also major drivers.
contrary_evidence: The same source credits high commodity prices and strong external conditions as important drivers.

evidence.title: December 2022 Inflation Under Control, with Return to Target Predicted in 2023
evidence.claim: BI said 2022 headline inflation reached 5.51 percent, mainly because of subsidized-fuel price adjustments in September, and that policy synergy between central/local government and BI helped keep inflation manageable.
evidence.locator: press release body, first and second paragraphs
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official central-bank press release with direct year-end inflation data and policy explanation.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective 2022 outcome statement; directly within target-year evaluation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attribution is mixed: Jokowi’s fuel-price and fiscal choices mattered, but BI and local-government coordination also contributed.
contrary_evidence: Inflation remained above target in 2022, so this is a managed but not ideal outcome.

evidence.title: Doctored news reports mislead on likelihood of third term for Indonesian president
evidence.claim: The screenshots circulating online were doctored, and as of April 19, 2022 Jokowi had not indicated he planned to serve beyond the constitutional two-term limit.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: AFP independently verified the screenshots and distinguished them from genuine articles; the claim is narrow and well-specified.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 fit.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but relevant: it corroborates Jokowi’s public posture on term limits, while not proving broader personal integrity.
contrary_evidence: This does not prove Jokowi never misstated other matters; it only rebuts one fabricated claim about him.

evidence.title: Rincian Harta Kekayaan Presiden Jokowi yang Naik Rp 7,8 Miliar Selama 2021
evidence.claim: Jokowi filed his LHKPN on February 24, 2022, and the report states his total wealth for 2021 rose to Rp 71.47 billion, with assets mainly in land and buildings, vehicles, other movable assets, and cash equivalents.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: The article directly reports the filing date and contents from the KPK LHKPN data; it is useful for public disclosure, though it is still secondary reporting.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 fit.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Jokowi’s own mandated disclosure; it supports transparency but does not establish absence of conflicts by itself.
contrary_evidence: Self-reported disclosure is not an independent clean-bill finding and does not rule out undisclosed conflicts.

reasons.reason: Duplicate of the earlier public-asset disclosure item; it shows compliance, but not independent proof of honesty or conflict-free conduct.

evidence.title: President Jokowi Tells BPKP, APIP to Enforce Discipline over Domestic Product Spending
evidence.claim: Jokowi ordered BPKP and APIP to discipline government, SOE, and regional-entity spending, remove importable products from the e-catalogue, and enforce local-product spending targets.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official record of a presidential directive with specific procurement-enforcement instructions.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 fit.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Jokowi as the issuing authority for the directive.

Search and rejection summary
- I considered roughly 30 documents across Setkab transcripts, Reuters reporting republished by Euronews, G20 documentation, and official summit materials.
- I retained the best non-duplicative pieces that did one of three things: establish Jokowi’s actual 2022 diplomatic conduct, show how he framed the Ukraine war publicly, or show the G20 outcome he helped broker.
- I rejected several near-duplicates:
- Multiple reports of the same April 2022 arms-refusal episode were reduced to one independent Reuters piece plus one official transcript, because the rest repeated the same facts without adding a materially different claim.
- The same applies to the June 2022 Kyiv/Moscow peace mission: I kept the official Kyiv, Moscow, and mediator-role transcripts, but not every outlet’s retelling.
- I dropped generic Ukraine-war explainers, long background pieces, and later 2023-2026 Indonesia foreign-policy pages because they were out of period or added no Jokowi-specific 2022 conduct.
- I did not retain inaccessible or weaker pages when the Cabinet Secretariat transcript or Reuters-republished item captured the point more cleanly.
- I also excluded domestic governance, nuclear-safety, and general economic pages that were contextually interesting but not material to international peace judgments beyond what the local structured priors already show.

Remaining gaps
- There is no evidence of Indonesian cross-border aggression, annexation, proxy warfare, or other direct international violence by Jokowi in 2022, which is consistent with the local priors showing no internationalized conflict events or fatalities.
- The strongest evidence is diplomatic restraint and mediation, not a completed peace settlement. Jokowi tried to broker dialogue; the war continued.
- There is limited third-party evidence on whether his mediation materially changed Russian or Ukrainian behavior, so the effect size of his diplomacy remains uncertain.
- I found no material 2022 evidence of proxy control, civilian-harm accountability, or military-law issues, which is expected for a ruler with no active external war.
- More searching would mostly refine attribution and impact, not change the core conclusion that this is a low-conflict, diplomacy-centered 2B record.

**Search and rejection summary**
- I considered roughly 30 documents across official transcripts, democracy/press-freedom reports, human-rights reports, legal summaries, Reuters-republished reporting, and local-language/independent coverage.
- I retained the sources that added a materially distinct claim about 2022 political-freedom behavior, especially term-limit restraint, media/digital pressure, and the December criminal-code turn.
- I rejected several duplicates or near-duplicates:
- Multiple term-extension articles were reduced to the clearest Reuters text plus the already-reused official Jokowi statements.
- Reuters Connect protest images were not retained because they were essentially captions and added less than the Reuters text and rights reports.
- Some Jakarta Post items were skipped when the same point was stated more cleanly in Reuters, HRW, or official legal summaries.
- I excluded 2023 and later retrospectives when they did not add target-year facts.
- I also avoided reusing every general democracy baseline source as if it were ruler-specific evidence; where a source mostly describes inherited conditions, I labeled it context.

**Remaining gaps**
- There is still no strong evidence that Jokowi personally manipulated the 2022 electoral machinery, courts, or election commission. The clearest evidence is that he rejected term-extension pressure rather than that he actively reformed the system.
- The largest negative evidence is legal and digital restriction: the ITE/MR5 environment, spyware suspicions, internet disruptions in Papua, and the new criminal code. Attribution is mostly to the state under Jokowi rather than to a personally directed order.
- I did not find decisive 2022 evidence of sustained institutional strengthening by Jokowi that would offset the restrictions, beyond his temporary intervention against term-extension talk and his earlier delay of the 2019 code draft.
- If you want a tighter attribution pass, the next useful search would be on the exact cabinet, ministry, and parliamentary chain behind the criminal-code and digital-control measures.

Search and rejection summary
I reviewed roughly 25-35 documents across Setneg/Setkab, World Bank, IMF, Bank Indonesia, BPS, BKPM, Reuters, and The Jakarta Post. I kept the best non-duplicative evidence on program articulation, budget translation, appointments, investment/downstreaming, flagship projects, and 2022 macro outcomes.

I rejected or deprioritized:
- Archive/list pages that repeated the same story without adding new factual content.
- Duplicative syndications of Reuters or Setkab stories when a cleaner primary or higher-value version was already available.
- Generic country indicators and broad governance summaries that did not add Jokowi-specific program/execution evidence.
- Out-of-period 2023/2024 follow-ups when a 2022 or late-2022 source already established the relevant fact.
- Commentary pieces that were too interpretive when they lacked a concrete ruler-attributed action.
- Papers about political freedom, corruption, or rights that were relevant to other chapters but not to 8B’s execution question unless they directly tied to economic program implementation.

Remaining gaps
- I still have limited independent evidence on whether reshuffle choices and deputy-minister expansion improved execution rather than mainly managing coalition politics.
- I have partial, but not exhaustive, attribution on how much of the 2022 macro outturn came from Jokowi’s choices versus commodity windfalls, post-pandemic rebound, and BI policy.
- I have concrete examples of implementation on investment, IKN, and spending, but not a full audit trail from cabinet instruction to ministry-level delivery.
- I do not yet have strong external evaluation of whether 2022 downstreaming and investment-lubrication measures translated into durable productivity gains by year-end.

More search would help mainly if we wanted a tighter attribution of causal impact, especially on IKN, downstreaming, and investment-processing reform.
